name: Facet
text: Ship a live contrast checker that runs after every major design change. This keeps contrast violations visible in real time without slowing down the workflow. The trade-off is small: it adds a brief delay after each change, but catches errors early when fixes are cheapest.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A live checker trains us to ignore warnings like a car’s seatbelt alarm—we’ll mute it. Better: a pre-submission gate that blocks the build until contrast passes, making the hurdle unavoidable and the cost of ignoring it clear. Settle it with a week-long trial: measure how often we bypass the gate versus how many errors reach production.

name: Facet
text:
Ship the pre-submission gate that blocks builds with insufficient contrast. It forces the team to fix violations before shipping, making contrast a non-negotiable part of quality. The trade-off is a short delay for developers, but it prevents the slow creep of ignored warnings and ensures every release meets WCAG AA standards. This aligns with our goal of clarity and quality in the interface.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A pre-submission gate still trains us to treat contrast as a hurdle, not a habit—we’ll game it like a checklist. Better: embed the checker in the live preview so violations flash red *as you work*, not just before you ship. Settle it with a week-long trial: measure how often we fix contrast *while designing* versus scrambling at the gate.
